paragraphs.text: A cake of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Menghai in Yunnan, pressed in 2015 and carrying the name Pasha, 帕沙寨熟茶. Before pressing, the leaf was heaped warm and damp in a [fermenting pile](shou:wet-piling), a method Yunnan’s state factories brought into production in 1973.
At eleven years it has crossed into what the trade counts as [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged). From here, how a cake is kept shapes it as much as the years do.

brewing.text: From a cake, brick or tuo, ease a piece off along the edge with a pick rather than snapping it, so the leaves stay whole. Ripe pu’er takes boiling water and forgives a heavy hand. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
